# $T_n\equiv\star3$ and $S_n\equiv\star3$ against nim heaps, for every even $n\ge12$ resp. odd $n\ge13$ (whole-board game on $C_n$)

**Summary**
1. Theorem (nim-heap outcome equivalence): in the whole-board game on $C_n$ (race rule "count", e.p. on, an e.p.-capturable pawn is not passed, game ends at the first passed pawn), the $(n+1)$-pawn rings $T_n = (B4\,W2)^{(n-10)/2}\,B5\,W2\,W6B7\,W3\,B7\,B6\,W3\,W2\,B6\,W2$ (even $n\ge12$) and $S_n = B4\,B6\,W3\,(W2\,B4)^{(n-11)/2}\,W6B7\,W3\,B7\,B6\,W3\,W2\,B6\,W2$ (odd $n\ge13$) satisfy: for every heap $h<256$, $G+\star h$ has the outcome of $\star3+\star h$ (P for $h=3$, N otherwise). This is written $G\equiv\star3$. The theorem is the heap test; H7 (section 3) says in what sense it gives the equality $G=\star3$ for the whole-board game.
2. The proof is the insertion proof of Section S13 (Lemmas 1-3 there, with the written-out Lemma 3 of Note 1 of Section S15, its section 2b), at one fixed cut per family: $T$: $c=4$, $n_0=20$; $S$: $c=7$, $n_0=23$. The $T$ wall is B4/W2 on files $0..n-11$; the $S$ wall is W2/B4 on files $3..n-9$, after the leading $B4\,B6\,W3$. Both are W2/B4 walls in the sense of type E of Section S13; no colour reversal is used.
3. C1 verifies the base graph and its arc: the reduced game at the base has 1305 nodes ($T_{20}$) resp. 40445 nodes ($S_{23}$), no e.p. flag, no passed pawn, zone $\{n-10,n-9\}\cup\{n-7..n-2\}$ resp. $\{0,1,2\}\cup\{n-10,n-9\}\cup\{n-7..n-1\}$, signature (the string of outcome classes in increasing heap order starting at zero) NNNPNN ($h=0..5$); files $c-4..c+5$ are exact pattern files in every node. H6 proves the insertion isomorphism at subsequent widths. C2: every size below $n_0$, i.e. $n=12,14,16,18$ ($T$) and $n=13,15,17,19,21$ ($S$), by direct search. E.p. convention: canonical (a flag only if an enemy pawn stands beside the landing square).
4. Status: PROVED for $n\ge n_0$ given Lemmas 1-3 of Section S13, 2b and the finite checks C1, C2; CHECKED-2 for the base cases.
5. The families are defined from $T_{12}$ and $S_{13}$. Allowing zero repeats gives $T_{10}$ and $S_{11}$. At heap 3 their outcomes are L and R, respectively. The separate twelve-pawn witness on $C_{11}$ is given in Section S6.

**How this note was checked.** The finite parts were computed by three independently written programs (section 0): A, the C program of Section S13, gave the reduced games, the pump and, through Lemma 1, the base-case signatures; E, a Python engine written from the rules, rebuilt the reduced graphs of C1, checked the hypotheses of Lemmas 2 and 3 on every node and ran direct searches for the smaller base cases; R, a Python program written from the rules by one of the referees (standard library only), rebuilt the reduced graphs, both insertion steps per family and every base case by direct search. Two earlier reports reviewed a prior version of the hand proof, one for the logic and one for the logic and the finite facts (with R), and requested or supported corrections that are incorporated in the text (most importantly, the theorem is stated as nim-heap outcome equivalence, H7); both referees were AI models from vendors other than that of the model that wrote the note. No human referee has checked it yet.

**Scope.** Proved: the whole-board game, race rule "count", canonical e.p. convention, and outcome equivalence to $\star3$ against nim-heap addends only (H7). Not claimed: outcomes with addends other than nim-heaps (H7 gives the sense in which the heap test is the equality with $\star3$), the component-sum model, another race rule, or equivalence against arbitrary addends rather than nim-heaps. Race-rule sensitivity and the component-sum model were not examined for $T_n$, $S_n$. The sizes $n<n_0$ are covered by C2, not by the induction.

## 0. Claims and labels

PROVED = by hand, given the lemmas. CHECKED-2 = two or more independently written programs agree. COMPUTED-1 = one program. Programs (sources in the code repository): **A** = the C program of Section S13, run through its four-family driver; **E** = a Python engine written from the rules; **R** = a Python program written from the rules by another AI model, standard library only, importing none of the project's game library or of the other engines. A drives the pump; E has a check driver and a base-case driver; R rebuilds the reduced graphs, both insertion steps and every base case.

## 1. Setting

Model, classes T/L/P/K, reduced game: as in Section S13 and in section 1 of Note 1 of Section S15 (race rule "count"). A **pattern file** contains precisely its one starting wall pawn. E.p. convention: a flag is recorded only if an enemy pawn stands beside the landing square of the double step; a flag nobody could use is dropped. "No flag" in C1, H4, H6 means this canonical convention. An inert raw flag cannot create an e.p. capture: a heap move leaves pawn locations unchanged and the next pawn move replaces the flag. Dropping it preserves play. Note 3 of Section S15, row S6 illustrates this for its families. Note 1 of Section S15, section 0, describes E's differential test.

Files $0..n-1$, $n$ even $\ge12$ ($T$) or odd $\ge13$ ($S$):

- $T_n$: $(B4\,W2)^{(n-10)/2}$ on files $0..n-11$, then $B5$ ($n-10$), $W2$ ($n-9$), $W6B7$ ($n-8$), $W3$ ($n-7$), $B7$ ($n-6$), $B6$ ($n-5$), $W3$ ($n-4$), $W2$ ($n-3$), $B6$ ($n-2$), $W2$ ($n-1$). The tail occupies 10 files and holds 11 pawns ($W6B7$ is two pawns), so the ring has $(n-10)+11=n+1$ pawns. **Wall** = files $0..n-11$ (length $n-10$, even), $B4$ on even files, $W2$ on odd files, $B4$ at the left end and $W2$ at the right end (file $n-11$ is odd since $n$ is even).
- $S_n$: $B4$ ($0$), $B6$ ($1$), $W3$ ($2$), then $(W2\,B4)^{(n-11)/2}$ on files $3..n-9$, then $W6B7$ ($n-8$), $W3$ ($n-7$), $B7$ ($n-6$), $B6$ ($n-5$), $W3$ ($n-4$), $W2$ ($n-3$), $B6$ ($n-2$), $W2$ ($n-1$). The tail occupies 8 files and holds 9 pawns ($W6B7$ is two pawns), so the ring has $3+(n-11)+9=n+1$ pawns. **Wall** = files $3..n-9$ (length $n-11$, even), $W2$ on odd files, $B4$ on even files.

Zone $Z_n$ (the files that change in some node of the reduced game). For the inductive widths the changed sets are the following: $Z_n=\{n-10,n-9\}\cup\{n-7..n-2\}$ ($T$), $Z_n=\{0,1,2\}\cup\{n-10,n-9\}\cup\{n-7..n-1\}$ ($S$). For $T$ the zone lies outside the wall. For $S$ the zone contains the leading files $0,1,2$ and the last two wall files $n-10,n-9$; the **fixed run** of $S$ is the wall minus the zone, files $3..n-11$. In A's $S$ scan the displayed zone and 40445-vertex counts hold at odd widths 19 through 41; the signature and zero-flag result hold at all scanned odd widths 13 through 41. At $S_{15}$ and $S_{17}$ file 4 also changes, although it is absent from the formula.

## 2. The cut and the base

Let $G_n$ denote the indicated whole-board game and $\Gamma_n$ its graph of K-reachable pawn positions, with a T-flag for each vertex and side having a winning terminal move. Terminal sinks are excluded from the vertex count. C1 establishes the invariant $I_n$ (H6) at $n_0$. Assuming it at width $n$, all files outside $Z_n$ keep their start content in every node of the reduced game.

- $T$: the whole wall $0..n-11$ is pattern in every node. With $c=4$ the arc $A=\{c-4..c+5\}=\{0..9\}$ lies in the wall iff $n-11\ge9$, i.e. $n\ge20$; it does not fit at $n=18$. Set $n_0=20$. $\mathrm{ins}_4$ fixes files $0..4$ and shifts files $\ge5$ by 2, so $\mathrm{ins}_4(Z_n)=Z_{n+2}$, and $c=4$ is admissible for every even $n\ge20$. Pump: insertion isomorphism $20\to22$ at $c=4$.
- $S$: not every wall file is pattern (the wall-end files $n-10,n-9$ are in the zone); the invariant used is that the fixed arc is pattern. With $c=7$ the arc $A=\{3..12\}$ lies in the fixed run $3..n-11$ iff $n-11\ge12$, i.e. $n\ge23$; at $n=21$ the zone files $11,12$ overlap the arc. Set $n_0=23$. $\mathrm{ins}_7$ fixes files $0..7$ and shifts files $\ge8$ by 2, so $\mathrm{ins}_7(Z_n)=Z_{n+2}$ (at $S_{25}$: $\{0,1,2,15,16,18..24\}$), and the fixed run grows to $3..n-9$ of $S_{n+2}$; the arc stays disjoint from the zone for every odd $n\ge23$. Insertion isomorphisms $23\to25$ and $25\to27$ at $c=7$ are checked by E and R; A's pump line for $n=25$ is its check of $23\to25$ against the previous size, at $c=7$.

The ranges are sufficient, not necessary: E's control cuts give exact insertion for $c=5..8$ ($T$, $n=20$) and $c=8..11$ ($S$, $n=23$), first failure at $c=9$ ($T$) and $c=12$ ($S$).

## 3. Hypotheses of Lemmas 2 and 3

**H1 (wall, phase, ends).** $T$: the wall alternates $B4$ (even) / $W2$ (odd), a W2/B4 wall as in type E of Section S13; $\mathrm{ins}_4$ inserts after file 4 copies of files 5 ($W2$) and 4 ($B4$), so the new files 5, 6 continue the phase; $\mathrm{ins}_4(\mathrm{start}_n)=\mathrm{start}_{n+2}$ for $n\ge20$. $S$: the wall alternates $W2$ (odd) / $B4$ (even); $\mathrm{ins}_7$ inserts $B4$, $W2$ on the new files 8, 9, continuing the phase; $\mathrm{ins}_7(\mathrm{start}_n)=\mathrm{start}_{n+2}$ for $n\ge23$. The leading files $0,1,2$ of $S$ are in the zone, outside the arc, and fixed by $\mathrm{ins}_7$. Both walls match the case analysis of Lemma 2(b) in Section S13 directly (Lemma 2(a) uses the exact triple; for Lemma 2(b), H3 supplies a five-file window, and H6 supplies absence of a flag), so no colour reversal is needed.

**H2 (no capture by $q$).** On a pattern triple, the capture squares of a $W2$ are on rank 3 while the adjacent $B4$ stand on rank 4, and the capture squares of a $B4$ are on rank 3 while the adjacent $W2$ stand on rank 2; so a wall pawn only pushes, and a $B4$ cannot take e.p. a $W2$ that has not moved (Note 1 of Section S15, H3). After a single step the neighbour is still ahead. After the double step $W2\to W4$ the adjacent $B4$ can capture en passant, so $W4$ is not passed.

**H3 (windows at the two ends of the arc).** In a step from $n$ to $n+2$ the central files are $c-3$ through $c+4$ in the source and $c-3$ through $c+6$ in its image. The following endpoint checks at the larger width concern that image. On the source central range use the right window for $j\le c+2$ and the left window otherwise. On the image central range the right window fits through $j=c+4$, and the left window fits thereafter. Each chosen window lies in the same alternating wall. Lemma 2 is local to the window, so Lemma 2(b) makes every central move L or P for every $n\ge n_0$.
- $T$, $c=4$: the central files are $1..8$ in the source $n_0=20$ and $1..10$ in its image $n=22$. Left end $j=1$ ($W2$), window $0..4$; right end $j=8$ ($B4$), window $5..9$ (at $n=22$: $j=10$, window $7..11$). E found 0 T/K moves at both ends in all nodes, every central move P.
- $S$, $c=7$: the central files are $4..11$ in the source $n_0=23$ and $4..13$ in its image $n=25$. Left end $j=4$ ($B4$), window $3..7$; right end $j=11$ ($W2$), window $8..12$ (at $n=25$: $j=13$, window $10..14$). At the right end (file 11 of $S_{23}$) E counted $L$ moves (28219) as well as $P$ moves (52671); Lemma 2(b) allows L, and there are 0 T/K moves. The wall-end files $13,14$ of $S_{23}$ lie outside the arc and outside both end windows. For example, E recorded T- and K-moves at file 14 of $S_{23}$.

**H4 (start).** $\mathrm{start}_n$ has no flag, since no pawn has just double-stepped, and no passed pawn. Every wall pawn is blocked by the opposite-colour pawn on a neighbouring wall file. $T$ core: $B5/W2$, the co-located $W6B7$, then the adjacent pairs $W3/B7$, $B6/W3$, $W2/B6$, and the final $W2$, which is blocked by the preceding $B6$. $S$: $B4$ on file 0 is blocked by $W2$ on file $n-1$ across the seam. $B6$ on file 1 and $W3$ on file 2 block one another. $W6$ and $B7$ on file $n-8$ block one another, and each remaining tail pawn has an opponent ahead on an adjacent file. E and R ran the passed-pawn test on all reduced nodes: none has a passer.

**H5 (race rule).** Lemma 2 never uses the race. The insertion shifts files but keeps every pawn's rank and the three-file pattern around the cut. In Lemma 3 insertion preserves passer colours, ranks, promotion distances and the identity of the mover (Note 1 of Section S15, H4). It preserves count, mover and opponent as local race decisions. The finite graphs and the theorem here use count.

**H6 (invariant).** $I_n$: no node of the reduced game has a flag, and every node agrees with $\mathrm{start}_n$ outside $Z_n$; in particular the arc $A$ is pattern in every node ($T$: the whole wall; $S$: the fixed run $3..n-11$, which contains $A$ for $n\ge23$). $I_{n_0}$ is C1. If $I_n$ holds ($n\ge n_0$): every node is non-terminal with no flag, and $A$ consists of pattern files, so Lemma 3 applies to every node with the chosen $c$; with H4 and induction on the distance from the root, nodes, K-edges and T-flags of $\Gamma_{n+2}$ are the $\mathrm{ins}_c$-images of those of $\Gamma_n$. An image has no flag; it agrees with $\mathrm{start}_{n+2}$ outside $Z_{n+2}$ since the inserted files are copies of pattern files and $\mathrm{ins}_c(Z_n)=Z_{n+2}$. So $I_{n+2}$. The computed steps ($20\to22\to24$; $23\to25\to27$) agree with this correspondence.

**H7 (meaning of $\equiv\star3$).** As in Section S13 and in H8 of Note 1 of Section S15, and as the theorem is stated: $G\equiv\star3$ means that for every heap $\star h$, $h<256$ (a passed pawn is worth $\pm256$), $G+\star h$ and $\star3+\star h$ have the same outcome: P for $h=3$ and N otherwise. C1 gives signature NNNPNN for $h=0..5$; for $6\le h<256$, the heap move to the P-position $G+\star3$ gives N. The start has no flag and neither do the reduced nodes, so the e.p. convention across a heap move is immaterial (E reported the same signatures under both settings, "keep" and "expire"; R directly checks terminality after expiry; on these roots the reduced graph is flag-free, so both readings give the reported signatures). Here $\equiv$ denotes the stated outcome test with nim heaps. Under the keep convention a heap move leaves the pawn position and its flag unchanged. Represent each resolved pawn position by its signed integer payoff $\pm256$. Against a nim heap this integer always has the outcome of its sign: the favoured side can move a nonzero heap to zero, and the other side can move only in the heap. Thus evaluation at a resolved position gives the same outcome as the ordinary disjunctive sum, and induction gives the same outcome at the root. Since $-\star k=\star k$, the checked P-outcome of $G+\star k$ is precisely the difference test for $G=\star k$ in this whole-board representation. The expire convention also gives the stated heap outcomes for these roots.

## 4. Finite checks

A, E and R agree on each base graph. E and R verify both steps at the stated fixed cut. A's first step uses that cut and its next step uses a cut one file farther right. The control-cut tallies and the numerical L/P split at file 11 of $S_{23}$ quoted here are from E.

- **C1T** ($n_0=20$; E, check driver for $T$, $n=20$, $c=4$): 1305 nodes, 4018 K-, 1212 T-moves, zone $\{10,11,13..18\}$, NNNPNN, files $0..9$ exact pattern in every node; Lemma 2: 10440 q-positions, 15660 moves, 0 (a)/(b) failures; Lemma 3: 1305 nodes onto 1305 at $20\to22$ and $22\to24$, 0 mismatches; control fails first at $c=9$ (1328 of 2610). A pump: 1305 nodes, zone $\{n-10,n-9\}\cup\{n-7..n-2\}$, ep=0, NNNPNNNN for $n=12..40$, insertion $20\to22$ at $c=4$. R: the same counts, zones and signature at $T_{20},T_{22},T_{24}$, exact insertion $20\to22$ and $22\to24$.
- **C1S** ($n_0=23$; E, check driver for $S$, $n=23$, $c=7$): 40445 nodes, 141252 K-, 86822 T-moves, zone $\{0,1,2,13,14,16..22\}$, NNNPNN, files $3..12$ exact pattern; Lemma 2: 323560 q-positions, 485340 moves, 0 failures; Lemma 3: 40445 nodes onto 40445 at $23\to25$ and $25\to27$, 0 mismatches; control fails first at $c=12$. A's $S$ scan: 40445 nodes and zone $\{0,1,2\}\cup\{n-10,n-9\}\cup\{n-7..n-1\}$ at odd $n=19..41$; ep=0 and NNNPNNNN at all scanned odd $n=13..41$; insertion $23\to25$ at $c=7$. R: the same counts, zone and signature at $S_{23}$; for $23\to25$ and $25\to27$ R recomputed the K/T children at every mapped node for both sides (80890 node/side pairs per step), exact correspondence and closure.
- **C2** (every size below $n_0$): E (base-case driver): $T_{12},T_{14},T_{16}$ NNNPNN under "keep" and "expire"; $S_{13},S_{15}$ NNNPNN under both readings. R: $T_{12},T_{14},T_{16},T_{18}$ and $S_{13},S_{15},S_{17},S_{19},S_{21}$, all NNNPNN under both readings (unreduced whole-board search; 763845 states at $T_{18}$, 15775446 at $S_{21}$). E reported the same signatures under both settings. R directly checks terminality after expiry. On these roots the reduced graph is flag-free, and both readings give the reported signatures. A gives NNNPNN for every one of these $n$ through the reduced game and Lemma 1. So each size below $n_0$ is CHECKED-2 (A and R), and $n\le16$ ($T$), $n\le15$ ($S$) also by E.

## 5. Proof of the Theorem

Let $n\ge n_0$ be of the right parity. $I_{n_0}$ is C1; H6 gives $I_n$ for all $n\ge n_0$ and $\Gamma_n\cong\Gamma_{n_0}$ (nodes, K-edges, T-flags). By C1 and Lemma 1, $G_n+\star3$ is a P-position and the signature is NNNPNN as in C1; H7 gives all heaps $h<256$: $G_n\equiv\star3$. For the sizes below $n_0$, $T_{12},T_{14},T_{16},T_{18}$ and $S_{13},S_{15},S_{17},S_{19},S_{21}$, use C2 and H7. $\blacksquare$

## 6. Gaps and caveats

1. **No gap found in the hypotheses.** What is new relative to the $M_n/O_n$ proof (Section S14) is the $(n+1)$-pawn tail with the co-located $W6B7$, the leading $B4\,B6\,W3$ of $S$ (in the zone, fixed by $\mathrm{ins}_7$), and the $S$ wall-end files $n-10,n-9$ in the zone, which is why $S$ uses the fixed-arc invariant and $n_0=23$ rather than the arc-in-wall bound $n\ge21$.
2. **Lemmas 1-3 are cited, not re-proved**; their hand proofs are those of Section S13 (in particular step (iii) of Lemma 3 in Section S13) and 2b, refereed as sound for $P_n$ and $Q_n$ (Notes 1 and 2 of Section S15). The proof depends on 2b, which is not re-proved here.
3. **C1, C2 are computer facts**: the theorem for $n\ge n_0$ is "proved modulo C1"; the sizes below $n_0$ are finite computations. A, E and R agree on each base graph. A, E and R are independently written (C, Python, and Python by another AI model). E's check-driver runs are E's independent rebuild of the reduced graph and the Lemma 2/3 hypotheses; E's base-case runs are E's direct search.
4. **The operational theorem uses $\equiv$.** H7 identifies its consequence for ordinary whole-board CGT equality under keep.
